title: MongoTemplate Queries
summary: Build conditions first, then limit, sort and select query results.

richText: MongoTemplate provides explicit MongoDB operations. Spring Boot configures it as an injectable bean.
Criteria describes a matching condition. Query holds conditions and options such as sorting and result limits.
is(value) checks equality. Conditions on different fields combine with AND.
Use repository methods for simple fixed searches. Use MongoTemplate when conditions depend on runtime choices or an update needs explicit operators.

richText: A regular expression is a pattern that matches text. Use equality when you need an exact value.
For a literal prefix search, quote the supplied prefix so regex symbols in it are treated as characters.
Keep field names and operators under application control. Pass input values to Criteria instead of building raw query text from them.

Pattern.quote makes characters such as . and * literal input.
The length check and result limit bound this search.
Index use depends on the pattern and query. Inspect query execution rather than assuming a regex uses an index efficiently.

richText: A result limit caps one returned list. It does not define page order.
Use deterministic sorting for pagination. Include a unique field such as _id when other sort values can repeat.
A projection selects only some fields. A partially loaded object is not a complete document replacement.
An index can help locate matching documents. Check query plans for the actual query.
For private data, include the authenticated owner in the query condition. Matching an ID alone does not establish permission.
